summary: Adolf Friedrich Stenzler was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Berlin, Greifswald, Bonn, and Paris under Franz Bopp, A. W. Schlegel, and Christian Lassen. He served as Professor of Sanskrit at Breslau (1833) and sub-librarian (1834–1872).

Adolf Holtzmann the Elder worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Othmar Frank, Johann Andreas Schmeller, and Eugène Burnouf, and served as Professor of German Literature and Sanskrit at Heidelberg University from 1852 to 1870.
Adolf Kaegi was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied under Rudolf von Roth around 1872–1874 and held a professorship at the University of Zurich from circa 1878 to 1914.

Adolf Kirchhoff was a linguist, historian, and archaeologist. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (circa 1842–1846) and later held posts at Frederick William University and Humboldt University of Berlin from circa 1865 to 1908.

Adolphe Régnier was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Eugène Burnouf. He held a post at the Palace of Fontainebleau and served as Professor of Latin Eloquence at the Collège de France from circa 1864 to 1884.

Adrian Zenz specializes in Tibetology and Sinology. He studied at the University of Auckland and completed his PhD at Cambridge under Hildegard Diemberger (~2007–2010). He held posts at CIU Korntal (~2010–2019) and the Victims of Communism Memorial Foundation (~2019).

Agata Bareja-Starzyńska works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She conducted research at the University of Oslo (1993) and the University of Bonn (1995), and held a post at the University of Warsaw (attested 2008).

Agathon Benary was a linguist who studied at Göttingen, Halle-Wittenberg, and under Franz Bopp. He held posts at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1831–1860) and as a professor at Köllnisches Gymnasium (~1832–1860).

Agehananda Bharati worked in Indology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. After studying at the University of Vienna (~1945–1948), he held posts at Delhi, Banaras Hindu, Tokyo, Kyoto, and Washington, and was professor of anthropology at Syracuse University (1961–1991).

Agnieszka Helman-Ważny works in Tibetology and history/archaeology. She studied at the Academy of Fine Arts, Warsaw, and completed her PhD at Nicolaus Copernicus University (~2002–2007). She held affiliations at Cornell University (~2008–2011) and the University of Warsaw (2015).

Ahmad Hasan Dani was a scholar of archaeology and Indology. He studied at Banaras Hindu University and the University of London under Altekar, Wheeler, and Codrington. He held posts at Dhaka, Peshawar (1962–1971), SOAS, and Quaid-i-Azam University (attested 1988).

Ajahn Amaro works in Buddhist studies. He studied at Bedford College and under Ajahn Chah and Ajahn Sumedho. He co-founded and served as co-abbot of Abhayagiri Buddhist Monastery (~1996–2010) and became abbot of Amaravati Buddhist Monastery around 2010.
Ajahn Brahm is a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar. He studied at Emmanuel College, University of Cambridge (~1969–1972) and later studied under Boonman Poonyathiro (~1974–1975).

Ajit Ranjan Bhattacharyya worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied as a pupil under Vidhusekhara Bhattacharya and held an appointment as Ex-Puranchand Nahar Fellow at the University of Calcutta.

Akifumi Naito specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Ryukoku University, Honganji-ha Shogakuin, and under Gadjin Nagao. He held posts at Ryukoku University, the Research Institute of Shin Buddhism, Kyoto Women's University, and Gyoshin Buddhist Academy.

Akihiko Akamatsu is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and linguistics. He studied at Kyoto University and the University of Paris/Sorbonne Nouvelle. He held academic posts at Kyushu University (~1986–2003) and Kyoto University (assistant ~1983–1986; professor ~2003–2018).

Akihiro Oda is a scholar of Buddhist studies who was educated at Otani University. He later served at Otani University as a full-time lecturer (attested 1992) and Professor of Buddhist Studies (attested 2013).

Akiko Walley works in Japanology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Aoyama Gakuin University and Harvard University, and held a post at the University of Oregon from 2009 to 2016.

Akimichi Eda specializes in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned a Dr. phil. at the University of Marburg under doctoral supervisor Michael Hahn (attested 2005) and studied under Katsumi Mimaki and Khangkar Tsultrim Kelsang.
Akio Donohashi specializes in history and archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1968–1976) and served as a professor at Kobe University (~1989–2012).
